resources.name: Biban / Entrepreneurship World Cup

resources.notes: Strong cohort source, but a finalist place alone is not evidence of software-buying intent.

resources.name: LEAP Rocket Fuel Startup Pitch Competition
resources.discovery_method: Official competition shortlist, agenda and winner pages
resources.harvest_instructions: Capture the shortlist and pitch-stage companies when published; prioritize Saudi headquarters or documented Saudi launches, then verify founder role, current product and timing from first-party pages.
resources.cadence: annual; check weekly during the six weeks before LEAP and once after the event
resources.notes: The official 2026 page says 100 startups pitch for a $1 million prize; use the roster, not the prize, as the discovery signal.

evidence.paraphrase: LEAP's official page describes 100 pitching startups, a public shortlist and a $1 million prize pool.

resources.name: Money20/20 Middle East Investor and Startup Programme
resources.discovery_method: Official programme, startup exhibition and pitch-finale materials
resources.harvest_instructions: Collect named startups from the official startup programme, pitch finale, exhibitor list and agenda; retain only Saudi-market operators and verify a current product initiative outside the event site.
resources.cadence: annual; check monthly from May through September
resources.notes: Useful for regulated fintech and embedded-finance discovery; event attendance is not a budget or outsourcing signal.

evidence.paraphrase: The official brochure documents an Investor and Startup programme and a startup pitch finale in Riyadh.

resources.name: Saudi Venture Capital Reports
resources.discovery_method: Official annual, half-year and impact reports
resources.harvest_instructions: Download each newly published market report; extract named Saudi startups, active investors and sector shifts, then use first-party company evidence to establish the founder, initiative and stage.
resources.cadence: quarterly, plus January and July release checks
resources.expected_yield: 20-60 company names and portfolio pathways per report cycle
resources.notes: Excellent market and financing context, but aggregated investment totals do not prove an individual company's budget or need.

evidence.paraphrase: SVC maintains an official library containing the FY2025 Saudi VC report and January 2026 impact report.

resources.name: RAED Ventures Portfolio

resources.harvest_instructions: Diff the official portfolio quarterly and check RAED's announcement pages monthly; research newly added Saudi companies for a specific launch, integration, product build or expansion trigger.

evidence.paraphrase: RAED's official portfolio page lists its companies and links to company sites, supporting repeatable identity and domain checks.

resources.name: Wa'ed Ventures Portfolio and News

resources.harvest_instructions: Review new portfolio cards and investment posts monthly; prioritize ventures with a named Saudi deployment, localization programme or current product milestone, then verify the decision-maker on an official team page.
resources.notes: Good for industrial and deep-tech companies as well as software. Filter out hardware-only opportunities without credible custom-software work.

evidence.paraphrase: Wa'ed's official site exposes a named portfolio and current investment news suitable for monthly harvesting.

resources.name: Impact46 Portfolio and News
resources.harvest_instructions: Check the official news feed monthly and portfolio quarterly; capture named founders, round details and stated use of proceeds, then confirm the product and stage on the company's own site.

resources.name: Wamda Saudi Arabia News Feed
resources.discovery_method: Country-filtered funding, launch and product news
resources.harvest_instructions: Review new Saudi entries weekly; use them to discover names and timing only, then open an official company, regulator, investor or founder source before promoting a lead.

resources.name: Arab News Startup and Funding Coverage

evidence.source_title: Saudi AI startup vminds.ai secures six-figure pre-seed

The current site supplies intent but not a dated 2026 launch commitment.

The public profile corroborates Amirah Alrehaili as Nuhieh co-founder and COO.

limitations: Abeer Tadmori's canonical LinkedIn URL was not confirmed.
No financing or direct external-delivery signal was found.

candidates.saudi_market_basis: Saudi fintech product presenting a Saudi-focused all-in-one money application and a public local company profile.
candidates.buying_authority: Named co-founder; current executive title needs exact-profile verification.

initiative.description: Building a waitlisted Saudi personal-finance application with an AI-operated founding model.

candidates.budget_traction: No public funding found; founder publicly stated the company had three co-founders and no employees, while the company profile reports a 2-10 band.
candidates.timing: Founder operating-model statement is recent and the product remains in a visible waitlist stage.

outsourcing_fit.evidence_basis: A founder explicitly reported no employees, which is a real capacity signal, but did not request or indicate use of an external software partner.

evidence.paraphrase: The official product site presents a Saudi personal-finance app and an active waitlist rather than a fully public launch.
A public co-founder post says urCASH had three co-founders and no employees and describes an AI-operated company model.
The public company profile lists Saudi Arabia, a 2024 founding year, a 2-10 company-size band and the urCASH brand.

limitations: The canonical personal profile was not resolved from the public post.
No employee capacity is not equivalent to outsourcing intent, especially for an explicitly AI-operated model.

gaps.description: Four candidates do not currently pass all four active gates. Raff lacks a first-party company or identity source; OORI has a current CEO-title conflict; Workey lacks a confirmed first-party domain and identity; Tadawulcom lacks a named buying authority.
gaps.recommended_action: Keep these records on hold and resolve the stated evidence gap before canonical import.

gaps.description: Canonical personal LinkedIn URLs were not confirmed for most named leads. Names and roles are retained from attributable public sources without manufacturing profile URLs.
gaps.recommended_action: Run exact-name plus current-company verification using ordinary read-only LinkedIn before promotion.

gaps.description: No candidate publicly stated that it wants an outside software-development partner. Funding, small headcount, an unfinished product and missing team data were not treated as proof of outsourcing intent.
gaps.recommended_action: Keep outsourcing likelihood conservative until a first-party build-partner, procurement, hiring-gap or implementation signal appears.

gaps.description: The principal financing announcements for these candidates are older than the preferred 12-month window.
gaps.recommended_action: Require a new product, partnership, regulation, hiring or financing milestone before treating them as timely active leads.

gaps.description: Funding stories and investor announcements often repeat company-supplied traction and use-of-proceeds language. These claims remain attributed rather than treated as audited facts.
gaps.recommended_action: Recheck material traction and budget claims against regulator filings, investor pages or current first-party product evidence during the verification wave.

gaps.description: Project Startup Saudi Arabia exposes useful 2025 showcase material but no clearly current 2026 cohort at the time of observation.
gaps.recommended_action: Keep the source on watch and refresh around the next announced edition.
